TL;DR: You MUST take this course from Prof. Stoltz if at all possible.
Prof. Stoltz is by far the best instructor you can take this course from. On top of being a very nice and friendly person, he is also very knowledgeable about whatever he is teaching and he has no issue in stimulating interest in the subjects. The reading material he has picked for this course are very interesting and enjoyable to read, and his friendly approach to students encouraged me to join in during the lectures since I genuinely enjoyed talking with him about the subjects we were discussing. He always gave convincing answers and praised any and every question he received, further emboldening us to participate. The short writing assignments he gave were very beneficial for learning and thinking about the texts we read and the midterm project pushed us to get creative with our writings, making it more enjoyable to write a paper than usual. I believe one of the most important and positive things about Prof. Stoltz is that he realizes the people he is reading the papers of are students from many diverse departments and thus, his expectations aren't very unrealistic, he rewards students for effort. His tailored feedback shows he genuinely enjoyed reading our papers and his enthusiasm to hear and read about our ideas felt relieving, making this lesson feel like more of a getaway from my other classes rather than yet another burden on my shoulders. I would only like it if he could make less breakout room activities since they were a bit inefficient, but overall everything was tremendous.  I'd like to thank him for a great semester, I hope you can also get to experience HUM112 in Prof. Stoltz' class.

This really kills the discussion environment and efficient exchange of ideas because the students who are not interested (generally the majority of the class) in the concepts never speak or contribute.
